data.title: IMF Sees UAE Economy Rebounding 7.3% in 2027 After War Disruptions — Market Talk
data.description: The United Arab Emirates' economy is expected to grow 7.3% in 2027 after expanding just 0.2% this year, assuming regional disruptions ease, the International Monetary Fund says. The Middle East conflict affected hydrocarbon production and key nonoil sectors during the second quarter, although oil output has since recovered. Hydrocarbon growth is projected at 13.3% next year, compared with 2.3% in 2026, while nonoil activity is expected to grow 5.4% after contracting 0.5% this year. Inflation is forecast to ease to around 3% in 2027 from 5% this year. The IMF expects the country's fiscal surplus to narrow to near balance in 2026 before recovering next year, while its current-account surplus is also projected to shrink significantly amid disruptions to trade and travel. data.title: Kevin Warsh's silence could be counterproductive
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 flat
  • Tech leads gains, defensives lag
  • Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq
  • Nasdaq futures rise 2.1%

KEVIN WARSH'S SILENCE COULD BE COUNTERPRODUCTIVE

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh doesn't like giving forward guidance about what the Fed might do, and while he might be following his own policy, his colleagues certainty aren't.

On BofA's stats there has been more Fedspeak in the last two weeks than in any period since the start of last year, and we've got six more speakers out today.

And in fact BofA wonder whether Warsh's refusal to guide markets might be encouraging the rest of the FOMC to speak more, not less.

"Typically, the Chair would weigh in, indicating to markets whether the hawks or doves are in ascendance. Absent this leadership, however, both sides might feel incentivised to speak more often and more forcefully," they say in a note.

Remarks by influential officials such as ​New York Fed President John Williams and Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson in the run up to October's meeting took a hike there off the table.

And BofA say, "Perhaps to avoid a repeat of this incident, the hawks have been very vocal of late."

Christopher Waller for example said on Wednesday the Fed either should approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

"The result of this back-and-forth," say BofA, "is undue rates volatility in already turbulent times."

data.title: Gamers dive into Grand Theft Auto 6 after the long wait
data.description:
Take-Two Interactive successfully launched Grand Theft Auto 6 late Wednesday night and into Thursday across time zones around the world. Sensor Tower estimated advance sales of GTA 6 to top 17M, with 75% of the sales estimated to be on Sony PlayStation consoles. The debut of the game is also reported to have broken livestream records on Twitch and YouTube .

For the company, the release ended a bumpy road to bringing the franchise back after a 13-year absence. However, GTA 6 landed the highest consensus rating ever with critics, which bodes well for Take-Two matching or exceeding its revenue guidance.

"Grand Theft Auto VI represents everything we have been working towards since we first started making games," updated Rockstar Games founder Sam Houser. "Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, we hope that we have created an experience that exceeds your expectations for what’s possible from this medium," he added.

Shares of Take-Two (TTW) fell 4.4% in premarket trading after rising 6.2% on Wednesday. Wall Street analysts have a consensus Buy rating on the stock, while Seeking Alpha analysts are more cautious with a consensus Hold rating.

data.title: Russian Arrested For Spying On Silicon Valley Defense Company Over Ukraine Support
data.description:
MOSCOW (dpa-AFX) - A Russian spy was arrested for targeting a Silicon Valley Technology and Defense Company that supports the Ukrainian military in the war against Russia.

A federal grand jury has indicted Igor D'iu on charges of conspiring to act as an agent of the Russian government, stalking, and fraud in connection with an alleged scheme to conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of the company.

The company is not named in charging documents, but multiple news outlets reported that the targeted company was defense technology firm Palantir Technologies.

According to the indictment and affidavit supporting the criminal complaint filed by prosecutors, in the summer of 2026, D'iu entered the U.S. illegally via the southern border after traveling through Istanbul and Mexico City,

The Russian agent was recruited by co-conspirators through Telegram, and he also received instructions and funds through the messaging platform.

'D'iu received instructions, equipment, and financial support from co-conspirators communicating with him through Telegram, who told D'iu his work was for 'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine,' the Justice Department said in a press release.

D'iu's assignments expanded to include surveillance of company employees and their residences. He followed many of them as they drove back from the company's Palo Alto office toward their residence in an SUV.

D'iu allegedly obtained fraudulent identification documents to conceal his identity. Investigators intercepted two international packages shipped from overseas that contained concealed identification documents, including a falsified California ID card, an altered U.S. passport, and a Social Security card bearing the assumed name of 'Hugo Landry Johns.'

In October, FBI agents arrested D'iu and at his residence in East Palo Alto, and recovered approximately $18,000 in cash, two laptops, two iPhones, two Russian passports, wireless networking equipment, and the fraudulent identification documents.

Following an initial court appearance on November 2, D'iu remains in federal custody ahead of subsequent court proceedings. He is next scheduled to appear in federal court on November 24.

data.title: France's OVHcloud launches AI cloud products hosted in Europe
data.description:
By Leo Marchandon and Emanuele Berro

OVHcloud has launched 55 cloud-computing and AI products that run on infrastructure hosted in Europe, including access to Nvidia's latest AI chips and a workplace application combining email, documents and videoconferencing with AI assistants, it said on Thursday.

European governments and companies increasingly scrutinise where AI services are operated and how their data is handled, creating opportunities for regional providers seeking to compete with US cloud and AI firms.

The French cloud provider said its data centres, which have 110 megawatts of free capacity, could take up to 60,000 of Nvidia's new Blackwell chips, which it said matched the largest global platforms.

For the past three years, OVHcloud has lacked the chips and reserved them for existing customers rather than using them to win new ones, CEO Octave Klaba said at the company's summit held in the Louvre museum in Paris.

The new services will be available on the state-certified cloud that already hosts the French government's electronic invoicing platform, the system at the centre of a nationwide reform in force since September, OVHcloud said.

Emmanuel Spina, head of state agency AIFE, told the summit the reform would spare businesses lost invoices and bring automated bill processing.

OVHcloud also announced partnerships with cloud-computing company Shadow, Qwant and EUSP, a joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia that develops a European search index.

Qwant's AI-generated summaries are already powered by OVHcloud's Olala model and hosted in European data centres, handling up to 3 million queries a day and cutting the search engine's computing costs to a third of what they used to be, the companies said.

data.title: Merck, Isomorphic Labs Enter Strategic Research Collaboration
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Merck will collaborate with Isomorphic Labs, an AI-first drug design company, to develop new therapies.

The companies on Thursday said they will collaborate to discover therapeutic small-molecule candidates against an oncology target of strategic importance.

Isomorphic Labs will deliver molecular designs derived from its artificial-intelligence-enabled drug design engine.

Meanwhile, Merck will provide data sets on which the drug design engine will run. It will additionally be responsible for preclinical and clinical development, as well as manufacturing and commercialization of any products derived from the collaboration.

"By combining Merck's substantial internal data capabilities and discovery expertise with Isomorphic Labs' powerful modeling and compute capabilities, we aim to identify new ways to design and create better candidates faster," said George Addona, head of discovery for preclinical development and translational medicine at Merck Research Laboratories.

Under the terms of the agreement, Isomorphic Labs will receive an undisclosed, upfront payment from Merck.

Isomorphic Labs will additionally be eligible for payments based on the achievement of specified research, development, regulatory and commercial milestones, as well as tiered royalties on net sales. It will also receive an option to co-fund development activities, in return for elevated royalties.
